subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What event sparked the 1905 Revolution when peaceful protesters were shot in St Petersburg?
questions.explain: Bloody Sunday in January 1905 saw troops fire on a peaceful petition march led by Father Gapon, igniting the revolution.

questions.q: In which month of 1917 did revolution force Tsar Nicholas II to abdicate?
questions.explain: The February Revolution of 1917 led to Nicholas II's abdication and the creation of the Provisional Government.

questions.q: What name is given to Stalin's purges and show trials of the late 1930s?
questions.explain: The Great Terror of 1936 to 1938 saw show trials and mass purges of party members, army officers and ordinary citizens.

questions.q: What happened to the Tsar and his family in July 1918?
questions.explain: Nicholas II and his family were shot by the Bolsheviks at Ekaterinburg in July 1918 during the Civil War.

questions.q: In which year did Lenin die, triggering a power struggle?
questions.explain: Lenin died in January 1924, leaving no clear successor and sparking the rivalry between Stalin and Trotsky.

questions.q: Who was Tsar Nicholas II's heir, the young boy who suffered from haemophilia?
questions.explain: Tsarevich Alexei, the only son of Nicholas II, suffered from haemophilia, which drew the family towards Rasputin.

questions.q: In which city did both the 1917 revolutions begin?
questions.explain: Both the February and October Revolutions of 1917 began in Petrograd, then the Russian capital.

questions.q: Who led the Bolsheviks and returned to Russia in April 1917?
questions.explain: Lenin returned from exile in April 1917 and issued the April Theses, demanding 'Peace, Bread and Land'.

questions.q: Which rival did Stalin outmanoeuvre and later have exiled and assassinated?
questions.explain: Stalin defeated Leon Trotsky in the power struggle; Trotsky was exiled in 1929 and assassinated in Mexico in 1940.

questions.q: What were Stalin's plans to rapidly industrialise the USSR from 1928 called?
questions.explain: The Five-Year Plans, beginning in 1928, set ambitious targets to transform the USSR into an industrial power.

questions.q: Which self-styled holy man gained influence over the royal family by claiming to heal the Tsarevich?
questions.explain: Grigori Rasputin won the trust of the Tsarina by appearing to ease Alexei's haemophilia, scandalising Russian society.

questions.q: Who headed the Provisional Government that the Bolsheviks overthrew in October 1917?
questions.explain: Alexander Kerensky led the Provisional Government by autumn 1917 but was toppled in the October Revolution.

questions.q: What 1918 treaty took Russia out of the First World War on harsh terms?
questions.explain: The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk in March 1918 ended Russian involvement in WWI but surrendered vast western territories to Germany.

questions.q: What official post did Stalin hold from 1922 that helped him build power?
options: General Secretary of the Communist Party
questions.explain: As General Secretary from 1922, Stalin controlled appointments and built a network of loyal supporters across the party.

questions.q: In the Russian Civil War, the Bolshevik forces were known by which name?
questions.explain: The Bolshevik Red Army fought the anti-communist Whites in the Civil War of 1918 to 1921.

questions.q: What was Stalin's policy of merging peasant farms into large state-run units called?
questions.explain: Collectivisation forced peasants onto collective farms (kolkhozes), causing resistance and a devastating famine in 1932-33.

questions.q: Which secret police organisation carried out Stalin's purges in the 1930s?
questions.explain: The NKVD, successor to the Cheka, conducted the arrests, executions and Gulag deportations of the Great Terror.

questions.q: What slogan captured the Bolsheviks' main promises in 1917?
questions.explain: 'Peace, Bread and Land' appealed to soldiers, workers and peasants and won the Bolsheviks mass support.

questions.q: What was the most famous Bolshevik newspaper, edited at times by Stalin?
questions.explain: Pravda ('Truth') was the leading Bolshevik newspaper used to spread party ideas and propaganda.

questions.q: What concession did Nicholas II make in the 1905 October Manifesto?
options: The creation of an elected Duma
questions.explain: The October Manifesto of 1905 promised an elected parliament, the Duma, and basic civil rights to calm the unrest.

questions.q: Wealthier peasants who resisted collectivisation were branded as which class enemy?
questions.explain: The kulaks, labelled as exploiting peasants, were dispossessed, deported or killed during collectivisation.

questions.q: What disastrous early defeat did Russia suffer against Germany in August 1914?
questions.explain: At the Battle of Tannenberg in August 1914, the Russian army was crushed by Germany, exposing wartime weaknesses.
